sql_schemas: table leave_request | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employee.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policy.id; approved_by -> employee.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups for 'my leave requests' per employee; status: filtering by status for approval queues and dashboards; leave_policy_id: filtering requests by leave type; approved_by: manager approval queue lookups; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection

table leave_balance | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employee.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policy.id | indexes: employee_id: per-employee balance lookups on every leave request; leave_policy_id: filtering balances by policy type; fiscal_year: partition-like access pattern — balances are always scoped to a fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint enforcement for one balance row per employee/policy/year

table leave_policy | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering active policies by leave type when employees apply; is_active: filtering only active policies for employee-facing queries

table employee | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employee.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for login and identity resolution; employee_number: unique lookup for HR operations; manager_id: team-level queries for manager dashboards; employment_status: filtering active employees for leave eligibility

table audit_log | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employee.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookups for a specific entity; performed_by: audit trail filtered by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering audit records by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, etc.)

methods: updateStatus(id: string, status: LeaveStatus, approvedBy?: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>
findOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId: string, leavePolicyId: string, fiscalYear: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
updateUsedDays(id: string, usedDays: number, remainingDays: number): Promise<LeaveBalance>
findByDateRange(startDate: Date, endDate: Date, params: AuditQueryParams): Promise<AuditLog[]>

data_notes: Persistence design for the leave management module. Five conceptual tables defined: leave_request (core leave applications with status lifecycle), leave_balance (per-employee/per-policy/per-year entitlement tracking), leave_policy (policy definitions by leave type), employee (referenced by all leave entities; includes manager self-reference), and audit_log (GP-002 compliance for all state-changing operations). Five repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by PostgreSQL via the existing pg Pool at src/shared/db/connection.ts. Index rationale reflects access patterns: employee-scoped lookups, status filtering for approval queues, date-range queries for calendar/overlap detection, and fiscal-year scoping for balances. The leave_balance table includes a composite uniqueness constraint on (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) to enforce one balance row per employee/policy/year.
